neighbours.label: The word cover/covered/covering/covers in its physical or spatial sense (a wall covered in paintings, a covered market, a town that covers 40 km²), not the reporting or insurance senses (covered the trial, insurance covered the cost).
fire: The hillside is covered in vineyards as far as the eye can see.
We ate lunch on a covered terrace overlooking the bay.
The national park covers almost two thousand square kilometres.
Every inch of the chapel ceiling is covered with gold leaf.
Thick snow covered the roofs of the village by morning.
A covered walkway links the station to the shopping centre.
The estate covers a total area of three hundred hectares.
Moss was covering the old stone steps down to the river.
quiet: The local paper covered the vineyard dispute for weeks.
We ate lunch on a sunny terrace overlooking the bay.
The national park is almost two thousand square kilometres in size.
Every inch of the chapel ceiling is painted with gold leaf.
The travel insurance covered the cost of the cancelled flight.
A long walkway links the station to the shopping centre.
The course covers the history of the estate in three lectures.
Moss was growing on the old stone steps down to the river.

predictions: 7-8/8 fire >= 0.30 (probes 0.50-0.61); reporting and insurance senses 0.05-0.06, synonyms 0.02-0.09.
notes: Probes (fraction of max 6.97): 'covers an area of about forty square kilometres' 0.614, 'covered in ivy and moss' 0.507, 'the covered market' 0.496.
